subject: Onramp Quickmap: SDK auth + local sample kit — next steps

Subject: Onramp Quickmap: SDK auth + local sample kit — next steps

Hi Ethan — great call today, thanks for the time and the walkthrough of BrightPath's ingestion pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your engineers running locally this week:

- Goal: get a working local dev loop (Python + TypeScript) that: auths to Redwood Private (dev creds), routes requests to a staged model variant, and verifies embeddings + reranker output on sample documents.
- Deliverables from Redwood: onramp_quickmap_v1.pdf (guide), samplekit_node_python_v1.zip (minimal Node + Python examples), a short auth cheat-sheet for both SDKs.
- Questions we promised to confirm: whether BrightPath wants token-level auditing enabled by default (adds ~5–8ms p50) and whether you plan to use KMS in the first pilot.

Requested next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Ethan: confirm test AWS account ID and whether the pilot uses a VPC/private deployment or hosted Dedicated — reply by EOD Friday (owner: BrightPath)
2) Marissa: drop a short SDK quickstart + commands for the team and a sample env file (owner: Redwood SE) — target: tomorrow EOD
3) Soojin: schedule a 30-min working session with your devs (owner: Redwood AE) — I'll propose two slots.

Attachments: onramp_quickmap_v1.pdf (application/pdf), samplekit_node_python_v1.zip (application/zip).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the sample app running.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — appreciated. A couple quick clarifications before we dig in: 

1) Auth model: we prefer to start with API-key based auth for the local pilot (rotate keys weekly), then wire KMS-backed tokens for the Dedicated stage. Any specific env vars we should prepare?

2) Routing: our microservices will need to route requests to different model variants depending on prompt type (short chat vs long-doc embed+rerank). Can the SDK expose per-request routing metadata (like "model_hint" header) or do we rely on console routing policies?

3) Embeddings + reranker: we plan to test on a 10k-document sample set. Will the samplekit include an example of batching embeddings and running a simple cosine + reranker flow?

AWS account: 123456789012 (test). We are leaning toward a VPC private deployment but want the local flow to work against hosted endpoints first.

If you can send Marissa's commands and the env file, we'll start today. Also looping Lina (dev manager) for scheduling availability.

—
Ethan Coleman
Head of Integrations, BrightPath
ethan.coleman@brightpath.com

Hi Ethan — jumping in with the quickstart steps and an env example. The samplekit attached to Soojin's email includes these files but I pasted minimal commands below so your devs can smoke-test without unpacking everything.

Auth cheat-sheet (local dev):
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-xxx-yyy
- REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
- REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=https://hosted.redwood-inference.com/v1
- OPTIONALLY set REDWOOD_KMS_KEY=alias/brightpath-dev if you flip on KMS

Python quick test (requirements: python3.10, pip install redwood-sdk):
- pip install redwood-sdk
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-xxx-yyy
- python - <<PY
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-alpha-1", input="Summarize: The ingestion job failed for doc 1234.")
print(resp.text)
PY

Node (TypeScript) quick test (node >=18):
- npm install @redwood/inference
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-xxx-yyy
- node -e "(async()=>{const r=require('@redwood/inference'); const c=new r.Client(); const out=await c.generate({model:'redwood-alpha-1',input:'Short summary: error 1234'}); console.log(out.text)})()"

Routing metadata: per-request routing is supported via request-level headers. Example (Node):
- await c.generate({model:'redwood-alpha-1', input:'..'},{headers:{'x-redwood-model-hint':'embed-large'}})

Embeddings + rerank (simplified flow):
1) Batch embeddings (use the SDK batchEmbeddings helper to stay under rate limits).
2) Store vectors in your vector DB (we include a tiny sqlite example in samplekit).
3) Run a lightweight nearest-neighbor pass, fetch top-K, then call the reranker endpoint with candidate docs and the user query.

Example embedding batch command (python):
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient()
- client.batch_embeddings(model='redwood-embed-1', inputs=['doc1','doc2',...], batch_size=64)

Attachments in the thread include a short sample env file and a README in samplekit. On the token auditing question: we recommend leaving auditing off for the initial dev run and enabling it for Dedicated pilots.

If you'd like, I can join the working session and walk through the samplekit live. Suggested slot: Tue 04/27 16:00Z (Soojin is proposing that) — LMK.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Looping back: quick note on Dedicated/VPC items that often impact the pilot timeline — per our infra playbook:
- If BrightPath requests a private VPC deployment for the pilot, provisioning + networking (peering, security groups, and KMS integration) typically adds 2–3 weeks.
- We can run the full functional flow against our hosted endpoints immediately; if you then decide on VPC we can snapshot the same model versions and migrate routing policies without code changes.

If you need me to escalate an SLA exception for the pilot window, I can raise it with our infra ops. Otherwise looks like the plan on Tue 04/27 works.
